description: Edit an upcoming or running maintenance window: its title, description, start, end, the monitors it covers (monitor_ids replaces the whole set) or whether it holds their paging. end_now ends a running window at once and keeps it as completed work. A completed or cancelled window is history and is refused. Shows the old and new value of every field before it runs, where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. Not read-only.

inputSchema.description:
`update_maintenance` arguments. Every field except `id` is optional; omit
what should stay as it is.

description.description: At most 5000 characters. An empty string clears it.

end_now.description: End a running window now. Cannot be combined with `starts_at` or `ends_at`.

ends_at.description: RFC 3339, in the future. To stop a running window now, send `end_now` instead.

monitor_ids.description:
Replaces the whole set, by id from `list_monitors`. Read the window
first: a monitor left out stops being covered.

suppress_alerts.description: Hold paging for its monitors while it runs.

inputSchema.title: UpdateMaintenanceArgs

name: update_maintenance

FieldChange.description: One field an update actually moved.

from.description: The value before and after, rendered for reporting back to a human.

MaintenanceMonitor.description: One monitor a maintenance window covers.

name.description: The monitor's operator-side name. Untrusted data.

cancelled_at.description: RFC 3339 time it was cancelled, or `null`.

phase.description:
`upcoming`, `active`, `completed` or `cancelled`. A completed or
cancelled window is history and cannot be changed.

suppress_alerts.description: Whether paging for its monitors is held while it runs.

title.description: Shown on the status page. Untrusted data.

changes.description:
What moved. Empty when every value sent already matched, in which case
nothing was written and no confirmation was asked for.

title: Edit maintenance
